= 6,590 (6.4 rpg) | stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 2,273 (2.2 apg) }} '''David Moorer West''' (born August 29, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played 15 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[New Orleans Hornets]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[San Antonio Spurs]] and [[Golden State Warriors]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier Musketeers]], earning [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|national college player of the year]] honors from the [[Associated Press]] (AP) and [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] (USBWA) as a senior in 2003. West was a two-time [[NBA All-Star]] (2008 and 2009) and a two-time [[NBA champion]] (2017 and 2018). ==High school and college career== West attended [[Garner Magnet High School]] in [[Garner, North Carolina]] and [[Hargrave Military Academy]] in [[Chatham, Virginia]]. As a senior in 1998–99, he earned first-team all-state honors playing for Hargrave. In his freshman season at [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], West was named to the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] All-Rookie Team after leading the A-10 in rebounding (9.1) and finishing fourth on the Musketeers in scoring (11.7).{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/david_west/bio/|title=David West Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 30, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140602035142/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/david_west/bio/|archive-date=June 2, 2014}} In his sophomore season, West led Xavier in scoring (17.8 ppg), rebounding (10.9 rpg, tops in A-10 and fourth nationally) and blocks (2.1 bpg). He recorded five 20-point, 20-rebound games throughout the 2000–01 season as West earned his first A-10 Player of the Year award. In his junior season, West was named the A-10 Player of the Year and the league's Defensive Player of the Year, while also winning A-10 Tournament MVP honors. He averaged 9.8 rebounds (26th in nation) and 2.5 blocks (22nd in nation) per game, and recorded the first triple-double in school history with 15 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists against Long Island University. In his senior season, West garnered two of the five major college basketball Player of the Year honors, being named AP National Player of the Year and National Player of the Year by the United States Basketball Writers Association. He became the first three-time Atlantic 10 Player of the Year, and was named first-team All-America by the Associated Press in 2002–03. West also became just the third player in Xavier history to surpass 2,000 points and only the second to eclipse 2,000 points and 1,000 rebounds, joining Tyrone Hill. In October 2007, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' released ''Sports Illustrated: The Basketball Book'', which featured West on its NCAA All-Decade Team for the decade beginning in 2000. He was joined by [[University of Connecticut|Connecticut]]'s [[Emeka Okafor]] and three [[Duke University|Duke]] players, [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jay Williams]], [[JJ Redick|J. J. Redick]] and [[Shane Battier]]. ==Professional career== ===New Orleans Hornets (2003–2011)=== [[File:David West shooting cropped.jpg|thumb|West in a game with the Hornets in 2010]] West was drafted by the [[New Orleans Hornets]] with the 18th overall pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]]. After recording modest production in his first two seasons, in [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06]], West enjoyed a breakthrough as he averaged 17.4 points and 7.4 rebounds with a .512 FG% in 74 games. That year, he finished second in the voting for the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]], behind [[Boris Diaw]] of the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/awards2006_improved.html |title=Phoenix's Boris Diaw Wins the 2005–06 NBA Most Improved Player Award |work=NBA.com |date=May 1, 2006 |access-date=May 2, 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320092124/http://www.nba.com/news/awards2006_improved.html |archive-date=March 20, 2015 |url-status=dead }} He also saw some time at [[Center (basketball)|center]], due to the team's lack of a true big man and demonstrated an ability to perform under pressure, as he converted three game-winning jump shots. In [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07]], West ended the season averaging 18.3 points, 8.2 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game. Despite missing 30 games due to an elbow injury, West recorded five games of 30 or more points and 13 games of 20 or more points. West again increased his statistical production in [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08]], and was selected to his first [[2008 NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star Game]] as a reserve, along with teammate [[Chris Paul]]. Paul later stated that he would rather not play with a power forward in the league other than West, because "he's not in it for the spotlight, all he cares about is getting buckets [scoring]." West reinforced his desire to be a team player in a 2008 postseason interview, saying that he does not care about being overlooked but would rather "play and be as effective as possible" while on the court.[http://sports.aol.com/fanhouse/2008/04/24/hornet-without-the-buzz-an-interview-with-david-west/ Hornet Without the Buzz: an Interview With David West] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080516051909/http://sports.aol.com/fanhouse/2008/04/24/hornet-without-the-buzz-an-interview-with-david-west/ |date=May 16, 2008 }} In [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09]], West repeated as an all-star and posted a new career high by scoring 21.0 points per game.{{Cite web |title=Veteran forward David West announces his retirement from NBA |url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-golden-state-warriors-david-west-retires-nba |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=David West Career Stats – NBA Regular Season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/2177/seasontype/2 |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}} On March 25, 2011, during one of the Hornets' last games of the season against the [[Utah Jazz]], West came down awkwardly after a dunk. The event occurred with 22.3 seconds left in the fourth quarter. West tore his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his left knee and was ruled out for the rest of the season.{{Cite Report}} On July 25, 2017, after winning his first championship ring, West re-signed with the Warriors for another year,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/six-players-re-signing-20170725|title=Warriors Re-Sign Curry, Durant, Iguodala, Livingston, Pachulia and West to Contracts|work=NBA.com|date=July 25, 2017|access-date=July 25, 2017}} with expectations to retire after the 2017–18 season.{{cite web|last=Maloney|first=Jack|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/nba-free-agency-veteran-david-west-warriors-agree-to-one-year-deal/|title=NBA Free Agency: Veteran David West, Warriors agree to one-year deal|work=cbssports.com|date=July 1, 2017|access-date=January 7, 2018}} On January 8, 2018, West became the 127th player in NBA history to play in 1,000 regular-season games, recording 10 points, six rebounds, and four assists in a 124–114 victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975343|title=Curry goes off again, Warriors top Nuggets for 5th straight|work=ESPN.com|date=January 8, 2018|access-date=January 8, 2018}} After reaching that milestone, West noted that he might consider signing again for the 2018–19 season, saying, "It all depends on how my body feels. Right now I feel good."{{cite web|last=Haynes|first=Chris|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22014538/david-west-going-strong-hitting-1000-game-milestone|title=David West still going strong after hitting 1,000-game milestone|work=ESPN.com|date=January 9, 2018|access-date=January 16, 2018}} The Warriors advanced to the [[2018 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] for the fourth straight season, where they won their second straight championship with a four-game sweep of the Cavaliers, giving West his second NBA championship. === Retirement === On August 30, 2018, West announced his retirement from the a more equitable system to "challenge the exploitation at the collegiate basketball level. ... Predominantly young black men, working, not being paid for their labor, and that labor being directly, monetarily beneficial for everyone but them."{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jWGQyWoPCcQ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/jWGQyWoPCcQ |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=Left Lens EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW: 2x NBA Champ David West on Black Politics & Nature of U.S. society|work=Black Agenda Report|date=July 27, 2020|time=45:35, 22:20, 19:55, 18:10, 37:10, 24:00, 25:55}}{{cbignore}} ==Personal life== West is the son of Amos and Harriet West.{{Cite web|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/2006/02/22/mr-clutchbrwest-has-become-hornets-go-to-guy/61899880007/|title=Mr. Clutch West has become Hornets' go-to guy|first=Jenni|last=Carlson|website=The Oklahoman}} He and his wife Lesley have one daughter, Dasia,{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/Licht_3Nov2006.html|title=In the Lane with Licht: "Mr. Clutch" Beats Buzzer Again|website=[[NBA.com]] }} and one son, David Benjamin.{{Cite web|url=https://hbleague.com/david-west/|title=David West – The Historical Basketball League|access-date=November 26, 2018|archive-date=November 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126162211/https://hbleague.com/david-west/|url-status=dead}} West is very interested in education, "black history, philosophy and various societal issues".{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/magazine_15mar2007.html|title=More Than Basketball: David West|website=www.nba.com}} He also loves to make mixtapes for his teammates, saying that it is a healthy habit that keeps him "in the house and off [his] feet". West has a Xavier "X" tattooed on his arm which displays, on either side, "My life, my way".[http://www.enquirer.com/xavier/2002/09/22/xu_five_questions_with.html Five Questions with David West] ===Political views=== In mid-2019, West appeared as a panelist and commentator on ''[[The Young Turks]]'' political news program to discuss [[Juneteenth]].{{Citation|last=The Young Turks|title=When Did You Learn About Juneteenth?|date=2019-06-19|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXSHZEq0mjc |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/AXSHZEq0mjc |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|access-date=2019-06-20}}{{cbignore}} In a July 2020 interview with ''Black Agenda Report'', West lamented the lack of understanding about China among Americans and denounced anti-China foreign policy [[War hawk|hawks]] as "warmongers."{{cite web|url=https://www.radio.com/sports/nba/former-nba-star-anti-china-propaganda-similar-to-iraq-war|title=Former NBA Star: I Warned Players Not to Support Anti-China Propaganda|work=Radio.com|date=July 30, 2020}} Regarding the NBA's rift with China following [[Daryl Morey]]'s tweet supporting the [[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]], West stated that the Hong Kong issue is more complicated than how it is portrayed in the American media, and that he contacted NBA players to caution them about being used as political pawns against China, stating: "I got on the phone with a bunch of NBA guys, and I was like 'Don't let them pull you into this bullshit, because it's the Iraq war-, [[Iraq and weapons of mass destruction|weapons of mass destruction]]-type propaganda again." Regarding the manner in which China is presented in the American media, West stated: "As people in the world, as Americans and people in American society, we have been misled." Concerning American politics, West expressed support for [[Medicare for All]] and stated that American society needs a fundamental restructuring in order to combat [[police brutality]], [[food desert]]s, and discrimination against black people in the healthcare industry. He stated that America has an "imperial lust that we haven't been able to get rid of," adding that "it has put us behind other nations in the fact that nations are united internally against the imperial wishes of the United States." West praised China for its improvements in poverty elimination, education, and life expectancy, and stated that China has "built their society in a way to defend itself against the constant imposition of Western imperialism. And in the midst of all of that, they have still been able to eke out some of the greatest advancements in human history. ... They've done it without war, they've done it without invasion, they've done it without bombing and blowing people up." He elaborated further that China demonstrates "there could be a functioning society outside of the control of the Western imperial power structure." ==See also== {{Portal|Sports}} * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball players with 2000 points and 1000 rebounds]] ==Notes== {{Reflist|group=lower-alpha}} ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{Commons category|David West (basketball)}} {{basketballstats|nba=david_west|bbr=w/westda01}} {{Navboxes|list= {{2003 NBA draft}} {{Golden State Warriors 2016–17 NBA champions}} {{Golden State Warriors 2017–18 NBA champions}} {{Oscar Robertson Trophy}} {{Adolph Rupp Trophy}} {{Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year}} {{2002 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{2003 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{Pete Newell Big Man Award}} {{Senior CLASS Award - Men's Basketball}} {{Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:West, David}} [[Category:1980 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:20th-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Bergen County, New Jersey]] [[Category:Garner Magnet High School alumni]] [[Category:Golden State Warriors players]] [[Category:Hargrave Military Academy alumni]] [[Category:Indiana Pacers players]] [[Category:NBA All-Stars]] [[Category:New Orleans Hornets draft picks]] [[Category:New Orleans Hornets players]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:San Antonio Spurs players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Teaneck, New Jersey]] [[Category:Xavier Musketeers men's basketball players]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]]
